title: Macroprudential and Monetary Policies in South Africa, Complements or Substitutes?
content: The article reports on the complementarity and substitutability of Macroprudential and 7 Monetary policies in South Africa, based on the interactions of both Business and Financial cycles. 8 To this end, a Dynamic Conditional Correlations and the Asymmetric Dynamic Conditional 9 Correlations MGARCH models together with the Artificial Neural Network VAR model, both linear 10 and nonlinear causality specifications, and the Structural VAR model were adopted for 11 synchronization, causality analysis and the analysis of shocks to cycles, respectively. Empirical 12 evidence obtained is such that, under conditions of financial and real economic stress in South 13 Africa, there exists high synchronicity and bidirectional causality between CBCI and CFCI. Hence, 14 Macroprudential and Monetary policies become complements, there exists interdependence 15 between the two policies and actions of one policy contributes to the improvement of the other. 16 However, under normal times there exist no synchronicity and a unidirectional causality 17 relationship running from CBCI to CFCI, was observed. Under such conditions, Macroprudential 18 and Monetary policies become substitutes, therefore independent of each other, hence, only one 19 policy can achieve the desired outcome. Overall, a shock to one cycle is a major determinant of the 20 fluctuations of the other cycle.
